This involved breaking down complex sentences into smaller, more manageable parts, and extracting key pieces of information. For the original research topic, the focus was on the functional requirements and design constraints. For the generated technical specification, the focus was on the described logic functions, signal behaviors, and module structure.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Counter counts from 0000 to 9999 and wraps around
ena[1] is the enable signal for the tens digit
ena[2] is the enable signal for the hundreds digit
ena[3] is the enable signal for the thousands digit
Ones digit increments every clock cycle when not reset
Counter resets to 0000 when the reset input is high
spec_atomic_units: Module defines a 4-digit BCD counter with a synchronous reset
clk input is the clock signal
reset input is the synchronous active-high reset signal
ena[3:1] outputs are enable signals for the tens, hundreds, and thousands digits, respectively
q[15:0] output represents the 4-digit BCD count
q[3:0] is the ones digit
q[7:4] is the tens digit
q[11:8] is the hundreds digit
q[15:12] is the thousands digit
ena[1] is asserted when q[3:0] equals 9 (1001)
ena[1] logic function is ena[1] = q[3] & q[0]
ena[2] is asserted when q[3:0] equals 9 (1001) AND q[7:4] equals 9 (1001)
ena[2] logic function is ena[2] = (q[3] & q[0]) & (q[7] & q[4])
ena[3] is asserted when q[3:0] equals 9 (1001) AND q[7:4] equals 9 (1001) AND q[11:8] equals 9 (1001)
ena[3] logic function is ena[3] = (q[3] & q[0]) & (q[7] & q[4]) & (q[11] & q[8])
reset signal directly affects the output q[15:0] when asserted
When reset is high, q[15:0] is set to 0
q output changes on the rising edge of clk when not reset
When reset is high, q is synchronously reset to 0 on the rising edge of clk
ena[1] goes high when the ones digit q[3:0] is 9
ena[2] goes high when the ones digit q[3:0] is 9 AND the tens digit q[7:4] is 9
ena[3] goes high when the ones digit q[3:0] is 9 AND the tens digit q[7:4] is 9 AND the hundreds digit q[11:8] is 9
The circuit is a sequential circuit with 4 BCD digit registers (16 bits total)
The registers are updated on the positive edge of the clock (clk)
The q output is declared as reg [15:0] q, indicating that it is updated using non-blocking assignments (<=) within the always @(posedge clk) block
The reset is synchronous, meaning that the reset signal is sampled on the rising edge of the clock
The ena signals are outputs of combinational logic that depends on the current state q
